name: The Provision Index
description: A nightly news program produced by Vantablack Media's subsidiary Meridian Broadcast Authority, presented with the visual grammar of independent journalism — rough cuts, on-location segments, a diverse anchor team — while operating under full Vantablack editorial control. Every story is technically accurate but framed through careful selection: labor disputes become 'workforce adjustment periods,' corponation evictions become 'residential optimization events.' The show's senior anchor, Adaeze Mirković-Sohn's former producer Yusuf Haile-Bergström, left the program in 2213 and has declined to discuss his reasons publicly.
cultural_impact: The show's visual mimicry of independent journalism eroded public trust in genuine independent outlets, as audiences increasingly couldn't distinguish editorial framing from authentic reporting.
story_hooks: Yusuf Haile-Bergström has a folder of unpublished scripts — stories he was ordered to kill — and he's looking for someone who can get them to a real outlet.
One of the on-location reporters has been quietly embedding factual corrections into the background signage of her segments for months.
A Tier 3 media literacy teacher is using The Provision Index as a classroom exercise in identifying manufactured neutrality — and has received a legal notice to stop.
